claims.wording: Why isn't Southeast Asia as closely knit as Europe? Historians give different answers. Anthony Reid writes about trade, and about Southeast Asia as a whole. Chris Baker, writing of the centuries before 1617, warns against maps that give Ayutthaya far-flung borders: its armies were used to keep trade routes open, not to set up firmer control.

claims.wording: Neither surviving account of 1612 is an eyewitness's. Floris worked from letters that his partner, Lucas Antheunis, wrote from Ayutthaya. In 1885 Ernest Satow found Floris contradicted by the Siamese chronicle, on dates above all; Floris's editor, W. H. Moreland, reports that Satow evidently trusted the chronicle more. Moreland answered in 1934 that the chronicle's dates had been shown to be wrong, and judged Floris's outline good evidence, from a merchant who had to know how matters stood and might err in details. The court chronicles survive in versions of the late 1700s at the earliest. Baker and Pasuk write that they were probably first composed near the events, have been rewritten over the years, and were most likely compiled to teach royal princes how to rule.
